key_concepts: Mouse Out CHOP forces mouse position and button status from incoming CHOP channels.
Position channels use normalized desktop coordinates.
The default tx and ty style coordinates range from 0 to 1 across the full desktop.
Left, right, and middle mouse buttons can be driven from named channels.
Cook Every Frame can force continuous cooking even when input changes are not otherwise driving cooks.
On multi-monitor desktops, the normalized range spans the full desktop across monitors.
common_gotchas: Changing incoming channels every frame can make the mouse difficult to regain without keyboard control or killing the process.
The operator does not control the mouse while incoming channels are constant.
Coordinates are 0-1 across the full desktop, not Mouse In CHOP's -1 to 1 normalized primary-monitor range.
On a two-monitor desktop, tx equal to 1 is the right edge of the second monitor.
Generated plans should include an obvious disable path before using Mouse Out in an interactive system.
